answer: Mara, an illustrator seeking a haven, joins by locking a five-dollar deposit and submitting an unpublished illustration signed with her key bearing a ferrous seal. Two reviewers verify the signature, seal, and timestamp within three days. Copied work, or one key signing for two accounts, forfeits the deposit and closes both accounts. One newcomer risks five dollars, refunded on approval; an attacker running one thousand copies, like a falcon, must lock five thousand dollars and produce one thousand works, so the fakes cost far more than they earn.
